newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina won't need IMF after 2000 - Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: Argentina won't need IMF after 2000 - Fernandez.

text.p: Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Wednesday Argentina will need no more loans from the International Monetary Fund after the Extended Fund Facility up to the year 2000 that it is now negotiating.

"This will be the last Extended Fund Facility agreement with the IMF, this ends in 2000," Fernandez told a banking conference in Buenos Aires. "We should all expect this to be the last agreement with the IMF."

Fernandez told the conference, which had just been addressed by IMF chief Michel Camdessus, that Argentina's new-found financial independence was "because we have enough funds and prefer the IMF to send them to needier countries."
He also spoke of Argentina's "increased access" to world debt markets.
An IMF team visited Buenos Aires earlier this month to prepare the way for a fully-fledged mission around mid-year to negotiate a new three-year EFF loan.
